channel.title: Majorca Daily Bulletin - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Majorca Daily Bulletin (majorcadailybulletin.com)

item.title: Video | Two dolphins spotted off the coast of Santa Ponsa
item.description: The video shows the dolphins surfacing simultaneously on multiple occasions.

item.title: Top British airline announces even more flights from London Gatwick to Palma, Mallorca
item.description: The airline and tour operator has also increased capacity for Summer 2027 to a number of popular destinations - Ibiza, Malaga, Palma and Tenerife - offering customers even more choice and flexibility when it comes to reaching their favourite hotspots.

item.title: Britons beware: Spain to ban the sale of energy drinks to minors under the age of 16
item.description: 25% of respondents consume energy drinks - on average, twice a week - that almost half (49%) of those who drink them do so at least once a day, and that 47% regularly mix them with alcohol.

item.title: Ryanair passengers flying from Spain reminded to check-in online or pay the penalty
item.description: “All Ryanair passengers will still receive email reminders to check-in online 48 and 24hrs predeparture. If any passenger arrives at airport but hasn’t checked in online (having ignored these reminders), they will still be required to pay the airport check-in fee.”

item.title: Balearic airports to create non-Schengen Britons only border control zones after new EU airport chaos
item.description: The aim is to improve the efficiency and quality of passport control, which requires the creation of a single area providing access to a non-Schengen boarding area.

item.title: Mallorca weather for Thursday, 26 February - Settled conditions due to last for several more days
Barcelona doubles tourism tax to one of highest in Europe
item.description: Manel Casals, general director of Barcelona's hoteliers' group, said proposals to raise the tax gradually to monitor its effects were ‌ignored. "One day they will kill the goose that lays the golden eggs," he said.

item.title: Palma town hall begins expropriation of shops in Plaza Mayor to kickstart redevelopment
item.description: The redevelopment project aims to improve pedestrian access and modernise the facilities.

item.title: Palma airport set for €621.6M revamp, including runways, terminals, boarding bridges and parking
item.description: Spain’s airport operator AENA has announced plans to invest €621.6 million in Palma de Mallorca airport between 2027 and 2031, representing a 46.7% increase on the €424 million allocated for the previous five-year period. The funds will be directed towards upgrading runways, taxiways, and parking facilities at the island’s busiest airport.
